analysis.title: Lula Shock Batters Brazil, Anthropic S-1 Revives AI Trade As Oil Dips Into Fed Week
key_insights: Monday Oct 26 opened calmly after last week's turmoil. Anthropic's S-1, Meta's equity raise and SPCX's debt issue supported AI names, and Neoclouds rebounded from an ugly open. NDX outperformed, the Dow lagged, and all US majors closed green.
Goldman's desk described activity at about 4 out of 10 with a 3% sell skew. Flow showed tech supply against consumer demand.
Anthropic's public S-1 lifted Nvidia, Broadcom and Micron. It shows a first operating profit in Q2 and an $80.7bn half-year net loss driven mostly by note revaluations.

Meta launched $22.5BN of Class A common plus $12.5BN of mandatory convertible preferred ($35BN total offering), followed by an ATM program of up to $60BN of non-voting Class C shares starting in 2027. Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicated interest in buying up to $5BN. The stock popped and then faded.
Credit rebounded modestly. Data center debt spreads compressed, hyperscaler CDS tightened modestly and IG spreads narrowed very slightly.

Brazilian markets sold off sharply on Lula's delayed surprise win. Multiple stocks fell more than 30%, a few more than 50%, banks and retailers were hit hardest, Brazilian rates jumped on expected government spending, 5Y CDS spiked and the real fell. Exporters Vale, Suzano, steel producers and Embraer gained.

Oil slowed its surge but stays near six-month highs on Iran risk. WTI closed around $102 and Dated Brent rose, which signals scarce physical barrels. Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials were travelling to Iran for talks, and Trump said it is 'getting to be decision time' on a deal or renewed attacks.
Rystad's Jorge Leon said the market is pricing some risk of escalation after the US midterm elections, which could keep prices elevated even if flows improve.
EU natgas topped €97/MWh for the first time since 2022. EU storage is about 75% full, the lowest for the season since 2009, and Germany is at just over 61%.

Treasuries were quiet. Yields rose from the open with the short end underperforming, then rallied in the last 15 minutes as oil fell. The 2Y auction was slightly soft, with indirect bidders taking 45.7% versus 57.7% last time.
CME data showed large Treasury futures position unwinds on Friday, including the biggest 10-year note futures de-risking since the December contract became most active at the end of August.
Options demand for lower yields further out the curve continues. Long-bond futures skew flipped to favor calls, with the largest call premium since February.

Markets price a Fed hike this week at about 10%, and December is seen as still in play. Investors are watching whether Warsh hints at anything at the press conference despite having sworn off forward guidance.
SPX's rally stalled at its 50-day moving average. Mag7 and the SPX 493 traded together, and AI outperformed ex-AI, which was unchanged.

Dealer positioning: MenthorQ shows SPX net gamma slightly negative and Nasdaq considerably more negative. The key SPX zone is 7,690-7,700, and a sustained move above it would materially improve the gamma backdrop.

Dip buyers are returning to AI capex names via longer-dated calls. The semi-index is down 21% in a month peak to trough, Nebius is down 39% and CoreWeave is down 43%. Bloomberg's Michael Ball sees these as defined-risk rebound bets that pulled NDX put/call skew off its highs, not a regime change.

Clean passage through the Fed and mega-cap earnings would lower implied volatility, bring volatility sellers back and move dealer gamma toward a stabilizing regime. Call-driven AI rebounds would add a vanna tailwind to NDX and SPX.

Bloomberg's view: positive AI guidance now needs compute pricing, utilization, equipment lives and financing costs all to go right. Cheaper tokens favor users over leveraged infrastructure builders, so being right on adoption does not guarantee being right on who captures the economics.

risk_factors: Escalation with Iran after the US midterm elections.
Fed meeting and Warsh's press conference could trigger volatility.
Hyperscaler capex justification, now that Meta is funding it with equity.
Negative dealer gamma amplifying index moves.
Circular AI financing and leveraged infrastructure builders.

EU gas supply tightness this winter.
vol_and_positioning: SPX net gamma is slightly negative and Nasdaq gamma is considerably more negative (MenthorQ). Dealer hedging amplifies moves, so volatility sellers have less incentive to step in.
Key SPX zone is 7,690-7,700. Above it, the gamma backdrop improves materially. Below it, AI rebounds face an unstable index.
NDX put/call skew is off recent highs as traders build longer-dated call positions in the AI names and other chip providers.
Long-bond futures options skew flipped to calls, with the largest call premium since February, as hedges against lower yields build.
Funds degrossed heavily last week and are not piling back into risk. Goldman's desk saw a 3% sell skew.
Treasury futures open interest showed large unwinds, including the biggest 10-year futures de-risking since late August.
Clean Fed and mega-cap earnings would lower implied volatility and add a vanna tailwind to NDX and SPX. Short-gamma positioning could see a squeeze.
geopolitical: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials travelling to Iran for talks, and Iran's president says he is ready to back any understanding and is not seeking nuclear weapons.
The Saudi coalition said it destroyed three drones in Riyadh, and Houthis and Saudi forces clashed over the weekend.
Reuters reported that Hezbollah is preparing for a new regional war after receiving funds from Iran.
Trump said it is 'getting to be decision time' on a deal with Tehran or resuming attacks.
The US has fully blockaded Iranian ports. CENTCOM says more than 1.5 billion barrels have passed through Hormuz with American assistance since summer.
Lula's delayed surprise win in Brazil's election hit local stocks, bonds and the real.

tension_points.bull_case: Dip buyers are building longer-dated calls in beaten-down AI names, the Anthropic S-1 showed a first operating profit, and a clean Fed plus earnings would lower implied volatility and add a vanna tailwind.
tension_points.bear_case: Funds are still degrossed, flow shows tech supply, Meta is funding capex with equity, and positive guidance requires compute pricing, utilization, equipment lives and financing costs all to go right. Cheaper tokens favor users over infrastructure builders.
tension_points.what_invalidates: SPX failing to hold above the 7,690-7,700 zone leaves the index mechanically unstable even if single-stock AI names rebound.
